description: Guided learning tour of the Julia programming language codebase, from CLI entry point through runtime, compiler, and standard library layers.

stops.title: Process Entry & Bootstrap
stops.description: Start at the C entry point where the Julia process begins. Understand how the CLI loader initializes the runtime, locates libraries, and transfers control to Julia's initialization.
objectives: Trace process startup from main() to jl_init()
Understand library discovery and loading mechanism
See how C API symbols are exported via trampolines

stops.title: Core Runtime Types & API
stops.description: Examine the fundamental C types that represent Julia values, tasks, modules, and the public C API. This is the contract between the runtime and everything above it.
objectives: Learn jl_value_t and the tagged pointer representation
Understand jl_datatype_t, jl_module_t, jl_task_t
See the public C API surface (jl_eval_string, jl_call, etc.)

stops.title: Garbage Collection & Memory
stops.description: Deep dive into Julia's generational garbage collector, memory allocation, and the write barrier. Critical for understanding performance and embedding.
objectives: Understand generational GC with page-based nursery
Learn the write barrier (jl_gc_wb) and remembered sets
See how finalizers and weak refs integrate
Understand allocation fast paths (jl_gc_alloc)

stops.title: Threading, Tasks & TLS
stops.description: Explore Julia's green-threading model: tasks, the scheduler, thread-local storage, and synchronization primitives. The runtime's concurrency foundation.
objectives: Distinguish OS threads (jl_n_threads) from Julia tasks
Understand task scheduling (jl_schedule, jl_yield)
Learn fast TLS (jl_tls_get/set) vs pthread TLS
See lock types: spinlocks, mutexes, rwlocks

stops.title: JIT Compilation & LLVM Codegen
stops.description: Follow the path from Julia IR to machine code. LLVM integration, pass pipeline, object caching, and the JIT layers abstraction.
objectives: Understand the JIT layer abstraction (ORC v2)
Trace codegen: Julia IR -> LLVM IR -> machine code
See the optimization pass pipeline
Learn object caching for compilation artifacts

stops.title: Support Library Utilities
stops.description: Platform-agnostic utilities used throughout the runtime: hashing, I/O streams, string processing, platform detection, and core data structures.
objectives: See cross-platform abstractions (atomic ops, SIMD, paths)
Understand hash tables used by the runtime
Learn the I/O stream abstraction (ios_t)
See string parsing and time utilities

stops.title: Compiler.jl — Type Inference & Optimization
stops.description: Switch to Julia code. The compiler proper: type inference (abstract interpretation), SSA IR, optimizations, and code generation. Written in Julia, swappable as a module.
objectives: Understand the compiler pipeline stages
Learn type inference via abstract interpretation
See SSA IR structure and optimization passes
Trace how Julia code becomes LLVM IR

stops.title: Parser & Syntax (JuliaSyntax)
stops.description: The modern Julia parser producing lossless syntax trees with precise source locations. Replaces the legacy flisp parser.
objectives: Understand green/red tree architecture
See tokenization and parsing phases
Learn how lossless syntax trees preserve formatting
Trace parse -> lower -> compile flow

stops.title: Lowering (JuliaLowering)
stops.description: Bridges the parser's high-level AST to the compiler's SSA IR. Handles macro expansion, comprehension desugaring, and control flow lowering.
objectives: See AST -> IR lowering rules
Understand macro expansion pipeline
Learn how comprehensions/generators desugar
Trace closure conversion and box capture

stops.title: Base Library — Core Primitives
stops.description: The standard library loaded at startup. Fundamental types (Int, Float, Array, Tuple), collections, I/O, math, reflection, and language primitives — all written in Julia.
objectives: Understand the bootstrap sequence (boot.jl -> essentials.jl)
See core type definitions and their C counterparts
Learn array memory layout and indexing
Explore reflection and method tables
Understand system image creation

stops.title: Standard Library Packages
stops.description: Independent packages loaded on demand. Each is a separate Julia package with its own versioning, tests, and dependencies. Key examples: Pkg, LinearAlgebra, Random, Sockets, Dates.
objectives: Understand stdlib package structure and loading
See how packages register with Base.require
Explore key stdlibs: Pkg, LinearAlgebra, Random
Learn versioning and compatibility constraints

stops.title: Build System, Testing & Development
stops.description: How Julia is built, tested, and developed. Make-based build, dependency management, test suite organization, and developer tooling.
objectives: Understand the build process (make -j)
Run tests: make test, make testall
Learn static analysis for C changes (Clang)
See CI configuration and performance testing
Understand contribution workflow

crossCuttingConcerns.name: Bootstrap & System Image
crossCuttingConcerns.description: How Julia builds a precompiled system image (sysimg) containing Base and stdlib for fast startup. See base/sysimg.jl and src/serialize.c

crossCuttingConcerns.name: C <-> Julia Interop
crossCuttingConcerns.description: Calling C from Julia (ccall) and embedding Julia in C (jl_init, jl_eval_string). Critical for packages and embedding.

crossCuttingConcerns.name: Performance & Optimization
crossCuttingConcerns.description: Type stability, inference, specialization, inlining, and escape analysis. The compiler's job is to make dynamic code fast.

crossCuttingConcerns.name: Concurrency Model
crossCuttingConcerns.description: Tasks (green threads), channels, @spawn, @threads, and the scheduler. Distinct from OS threads.
